title: Timeout allocator and pool shaping recipes for Python/TS/Go SDKs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Users see inconsistent tail-latency and transient failures across Python/TS/Go SDKs when hitting Redwood APIs with mixed workloads (short control calls, long-generative requests, streaming). Causes: per-language defaults diverged, pools exhaust on connection storms, and retry semantics interact poorly with streaming re-connects. This ticket defines a cross-SDK "timeout allocator" pattern plus pool shaping recipes and streaming ergonomics guidelines, with concrete per-language examples, telemetry signals, and rollout steps.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Default timeout allocator implemented in Python/TS/Go SDKs behind a feature flag; SDKs choose sensible deadlines for interactive vs batch calls.
A2: Connection pool shaping presets (small/medium/large) implemented with documented parameters (max_idle, max_active, per-route leases) and runtime hints exposed.
A3: Streaming ergonomics: client-side resumable streams + backpressure-aware reconnect logic added to SDKs and example code provided.
A4: End-to-end tests and load profiles demonstrating at least 30% reduction in tail p99 for control calls under mixed load compared to current defaults.
A5: Telemetry dashboards and alerts for pool saturation, retry storms, and disconnect-reconnect cycles live in Console before rollout to GA defaults.
A6: Docs and migration guide published; breaking changes behind opt-in flags for one release cycle.
A7: Security review: non-applicable (no new auth surface) or completed if KMS/HSM integration referenced in followups.
design_notes: Problem decomposition: separate concerns into (1) timeout allocator (per-route/mode deadlines), (2) pool shaping presets, (3) streaming reconnect semantics, (4) telemetry & heuristics for automatic suggestions.

Timeout allocator: SDK exposes a small policy DSL: {mode: interactive|background|streaming, base: ms, jitter_pct, hedging_allowed}. The allocator synthesizes a client deadline = base * route_factor * user_hint, and provides an early-fail signal for long-tail CPU/GPU stalls.

Pool shaping: define three presets (dev-light, prod-balanced, prod-high-throughput). Key knobs: max_active, max_idle, connection_ttl, idle_reap_interval, per_host_shard_count. Default chosen per SDK based on typical runtime (node event loop, python async, go goroutines).

Streaming ergonomics: require resumable tokens (server-provided opaque resume cursor) for long-lived streams. On transient network errors, client will perform exponential backoff with jitter, resume with last-acked token, and limit in-flight reconnect attempts to avoid herd retries.

Retries and interaction: retriable idempotent RPCs vs non-idempotent streaming messages. Retries should be layered: short internal hedges for latency-sensitive reads, and longer scheduled retries for background tasks. Expose a simple retry_policy object with max_attempts, per-attempt_deadline, and overall_budget_ms.
Telemetry: emit events for PoolSaturation, ConnRecycle, RetryBudgetExhausted, StreamResumeSuccess/Fail, and DeadlineApplied (value). These enable Console recommendations and Optimize suggestions.
Migration: opt-in feature flag (sdk.timeout_allocator=v1) for 1 minor release; default flip after metrics validate. Provide quick revert flag for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers.
Tradeoffs: aggressive idle recycling reduces file descriptors but increases reconnect churn; we recommend conservative defaults and a recommended aggressive preset for burst workloads.
Security: no secrets introduced. Resume tokens are opaque; verify length/entropy and rotate as part of session lifecycle if needed.
examples:
Python (async) example:
from redwood import RedwoodClient
from redwood.transport import TimeoutAllocator, PoolPreset

allocator = TimeoutAllocator(mode="interactive", base_ms=400, jitter_pct=10)
client = RedwoodClient(timeout_allocator=allocator, pool_preset=PoolPreset.PROD_BALANCED)

# short control call gets small deadline
resp = await client.text.generate(prompt="ping")

Go example (context-aware):
alloc := transport.NewAllocator(transport.ModeInteractive, 350*time.Millisecond, 0.10)
client := redwood.NewClient(redwood.WithAllocator(alloc), redwood.WithPoolPreset(redwood.PresetProdBalanced))
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), alloc.DeadlineForRoute('/v1/generate'))
defer cancel()
resp, err := client.Generate(ctx, req)

Streaming reconnect recipe:
1) On transient error, record last-ack/resume-token.
2) Do exponential backoff (base 200ms, factor 2, jitter 0.2) up to 10s.
3) Attempt resume with token; if resume rejected, fall back to checkpointed state rebuild or full restart with user-visible error after 3 attempts.
4) Emit StreamResumeSuccess/Fail telemetry and traces.
telemetry: Events to emit: DeadlineApplied(route, ms, mode), PoolSaturation(route, preset, pct), ConnRecycle(route, reason), RetryAttempt(route, outcome), StreamResumeAttempt(success:boolean)
Metrics: pool_active_count, pool_idle_count, conn_reconnect_rate, retry_budget_remaining, p50/p95/p99 latency per mode (interactive/background/streaming)
Dashboard: per-customer heatmap of pool saturation + suggestions engine that recommends preset changes and timeout adjustments when tail latency rises >25% vs baseline
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator arithmetic, jitter, and boundary conditions across SDKs.
Integration tests: simulated server delays to validate deadlines and early-fail behavior, and simulated connection storms to validate pool shaping prevents global FDs exhaustion.
Load tests: mixed workload (80% short control calls, 20% long streams) to prove p99 improvements and measure retry storms. Use existing perf harness (link below).
Chaos tests: inject network blips and verify streaming resume semantics and that retry budgets prevent herd behavior.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: implement behind feature flags in SDK branches and add e2e tests (2 weeks).
Stage 1: internal dogfood with Redwood services and infra team using prod-balanced preset (1 week). Collect telemetry.
Stage 2: beta opt-in release to customers with a 'transport-preview' banner and migration docs (2 weeks).
Stage 3: GA default flip after metrics validation and one release cycle; provide rollback flag and enterprise advisory notes.
